chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Saif ibn Umayra, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira ibn al-Nasri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And (it is) an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage»

He said: It is a name whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gifted to Ali, Allah’s blessings be upon him, from the Heaven, because he was, indeed, the one who delivered on behalf of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, (the chapter of) Bara’a

He had sent it with Abu Bakr at first, at which Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, descended unto him and said: «O Muhammed, indeed, Allah says to you: Indeed, none shall deliver on behalf of you except for you or a man from you»

Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, sent Ali, peace be upon him, therein, and so he caught up with Abu Bakr, took the journal from his hand and went with it to Mecca
Allah then named it an Announcement from Allah. It is, indeed, a name gifted by Allah from the Heaven to Ali, peace be upon him.

key_terms.أَذَانٌ: Announcement or proclamation, here interpreted as a specific title or role attributed to Ali.
key_terms.الصَّحِيفَةَ: The scroll or document containing the Quranic chapter being delivered.
key_terms.بَرَاءَةٌ: The chapter of Surah al-Bara'a (Declaration of Disavowal) from the Quran, specifically delivered to the people of Mecca.
key_terms.جِبْرِئِيلُ: The Archangel Gabriel, who conveyed the divine instruction regarding who should deliver the message.
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Day of the Greater Pilgrimage, a specific occasion in Islamic history associated with the final proclamation of the Quranic verse.

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Allah' referred to in the phrase 'an announcement from Allah and His Messenger' in Surah al-Tawbah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents a distinctive Shia interpretation where the term 'Allah' in the phrase 'announcement from Allah and His Messenger' (9:3) refers specifically to Ali ibn Abi Talib, designating him as the divine announcer. The narration details how Gabriel instructed the Prophet to send only Ali to deliver the Scroll of Disavowal to Abu Bakr, thereby elevating Ali’s role from mere courier to the embodiment of the divine message itself. This highlights the Shia belief in Ali’s unique authority and proximity to the Prophet in conveying critical religious decrees.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammed bin Hussain bin Abi’l-Khattab, from Ali bin Asbat, from Saif bin ‘Umayra, from Harith bin Mughaira bin Nasri, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And (it is) an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage» [9:3].

He said: It is a name whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gifted to Ali, Allah’s blessings be upon him, from the Heaven, because he was, indeed, the one who delivered on behalf of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, (the chapter of) Bara’a [1].

He had sent it with Abu Bakr at first, at which Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, descended unto him and said: «O Muhammed, indeed, Allah says to you: Indeed, none shall deliver on behalf of you except for you or a man from you».

Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, sent Ali, peace be upon him, therein, and so he caught up with Abu Bakr, took the journal from his hand and went with it to Mecca.
Allah then named it an Announcement from Allah. It is, indeed, a name gifted by Allah from the Heaven to Ali, peace be upon him.
